Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
1003 AM PST Thu Nov 26 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Widespread coastal flooding is expected to continue into Friday 
due to King Tides and increased surf. Warmer for today and Friday
with high temperatures as warm as the lower to mid 80s for inland
coastal areas into the western valleys. Offshore lower-level flow
will bring gusty east to northeast winds along and below the 
coastal slopes of the mountains today with gusts to around 35 mph.
Cooling will spread inland for Saturday through Wednesday. There 
is a 50 percent chance for showers from the coast to the mountains
for Sunday night and Monday. Chances for rainfall and heavier 
rainfall will increase significantly for Tuesday and Wednesday as 
a strong Pacific storm moves inland into California.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...


...UPDATED AVIATION, MARINE, AND BEACHES DISCUSSION...

.SHORT TERM (Today through Saturday)...
High pressure aloft will strengthen for today and Friday. Offshore
lower-level flow will bring gusty east to northeast winds along
and below the coastal slopes of the mountains today with gusts to
around 35 mph.

High temperatures for today will warm as much as 8 to 12 degrees
for the valleys and inland coastal areas. High temperatures for
today will be as much as 12 to 18 degrees above average for the
coast and western valleys. Warmest high temperatures, in the
lower to mid 80s, will be in inland coastal areas into the western
valleys. High temperatures on Friday will warm another 5 degrees
for the mountains and high desert.

On Saturday, high pressure aloft will begin to weaken and onshore
lower-level flow will return. Cooling will begin to spread inland
with cooling of 4 to 8 degrees for the coast to the coastal slopes
of the mountains. High temperatures for the coast and valleys will
be mostly in the mid 70s to around 80 with the lower deserts in
the lower to mid 80s and the mountains in the mid 50s to mid 70s.

&&

.LONG TERM (Sunday through Wednesday)...
The cooling trend will continue through Wednesday with high
temperatures on Wednesday as much as 4 to 8 degrees below average
for the mountains and inland valleys. For the coast and valleys, 
high temperatures will range from the lower 60s for the far inland
valleys to the upper 60s for coastal areas.

Chances for measurable rainfall will remain below 10 percent
through Sunday, then increase to around 50 percent from the coast
to the mountains for Sunday night through Monday, but with the 
chance for 0.25 inch or more only 15 to 25 percent.

Chances for rainfall and heavier rainfall will increase
significantly for Tuesday and Wednesday as a strong Pacific storm
moves inland into California with the chance of 1 inch or more of
rainfall from the coast to the mountains for Tuesday morning
through Wednesday night of 75 to 85 percent. The chance for 3 
inches or more of rainfall ranges from less than 10 percent near 
the coast to as high as 35 to 45 percent in the mountains of San 
Bernardino County.

The latest model track and timing would bring the most significant
impacts into southwestern California for late Tuesday and Tuesday 
night. Those impacts would also include strong winds and a chance 
of thunderstorms over the coastal waters into coastal areas.

&&

.AVIATION... 
261800Z...VFR prevailing with SKC. Northeast winds with gusts 25-35 
kts along coastal slopes and through passes, decreasing around 22z. 
SCT-BKN high clouds AOA 20kft moves in this evening/early Friday 
morning with lighter winds.

&&

.MARINE...
Combined seas of 7 to 10 feet in the outer coastal waters south of 
San Clemente Island will continue through the morning. Seas lower 
this afternoon, falling below 8 feet by this evening.

&&

.BEACHES...
The La Jolla tide gauge recorded a high tide of 8.11 ft MLLW 
Wednesday morning, preliminarily breaking the all-time record just 
recently set on October 27th. King Tides continue today, and have 
peaked just below 8 ft this morning. Forecast tides have been 
adjusted 1.1-1.2 feet above baseline astronomical predictions based 
on trends in recent observations. 

A long period west swell of 7-9 ft at 16-18 seconds is generating 
large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, with sets of 10-12 feet on exposed 
west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-5 feet with local sets to 7 
feet on Friday. A High Surf Advisory is in effect for San Diego 
County through 4 AM Friday with the swell focusing the higher surf 
on the west-facing beaches.

The combination of forecast record King Tides and elevated to high 
surf will bring moderate to major coastal flooding, with locally 
extreme flooding expected during this morning's high tide. A Coastal 
Flood Warning remains in effect through early Friday afternoon.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.


&&

     Coastal Areas-San Diego County Coastal Areas.

     High Surf Advisory until 4 AM PST Friday for San Diego County 
     Coastal Areas.
